# #634 — flaky: wall-clock timing assertions fail non-deterministically under CI load (3 different tests in 3 runs)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-08T06:56:42Z
Updated: 2026-08-08T06:56:42Z

---

## Symptom

CI's `check` job fails intermittently, with a **different** test each run, on branches whose diffs cannot plausibly affect them. Three consecutive runs on PR #629 (a diff touching only `.claude/hooks/`, `scripts/`, and `.claude/settings.json` — zero `src/`, zero `server/`):

| Run | Failure |
|---|---|
| 1 | `0 fail`, `1 error` — unhandled `proc.kill is not a function` at `src/tools/search-all.ts:110` (filed as #632) |
| 2 | `1 fail` — `session lifecycle event bounds (#515)`, `a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out`, exactly `5000.98ms` |
| 3 | `1 fail` — `ob-backfill sanitize > scans token-dense transcripts without quadratic blowup`, `1274.00ms` |

## Root cause: wall-clock assertions on shared CI hardware

`scripts/ob-backfill.test.ts:259`:

```ts
expect(performance.now() - startedAt).toBeLessThan(1_000);
```

This asserts a **wall-clock duration**, so it measures the runner's current load as much as the code's complexity. It failed at 1274ms — 27% over a threshold that has nothing to do with correctness. The `session-lifecycle.pg` failure is the same shape at the hook level: a 5000ms `beforeEach`/`afterEach` bound, hit exactly, i.e. timed out rather than errored.

## Differential proof (per the #609 standard)

Both failing tests were run against **PR #629's exact head content** in a fresh worktree with a fresh migrated database:

```
server/tools/session-lifecycle.pg.test.ts   4 pass, 0 fail
scripts/ob-backfill.test.ts                22 pass, 0 fail
```

So neither failure is reproducible from the code under test. `main`'s own recent CI runs are green, which is why these are NOT being labelled "pre-existing" — the honest label is **load-sensitive and non-deterministic**.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than re-running

A suite that fails on a different unrelated test each run trains every lane to re-run CI until it is green, which is indistinguishable from the habit that lets a *real* failure through. It also makes red CI uninformative exactly when a controller is deciding whether to merge.

Suggested direction: assert on the property the test actually cares about — complexity/behaviour (e.g. operation counts, or a ratio between two input sizes) rather than absolute elapsed milliseconds on shared hardware.
